questions.question: A fridge has a cash price of R9 499. The HP deal asks a 15% deposit and 30 monthly instalments of R379,90. Calculate the total HP price and the extra paid compared with cash, and explain how lay-by would differ for the same fridge.
questions.expected_answer: The deposit is 15% of 9 499, which is R1 424,85. The instalments total 379,90 × 30 = R11 397,00. The total HP price is deposit plus instalments: 1 424,85 + 11 397,00 = R12 821,85. The extra paid for buying on HP is 12 821,85 − 9 499 = R3 322,85, about 35% above the cash price — this extra is the interest and charges of the agreement, and until the final instalment the store still owns the fridge. Lay-by charges no interest: the buyer pays the exact cash price of R9 499 in instalments, about R1 900 a month over five months, but only receives the fridge once the final payment is made. HP sells immediate possession at a premium; lay-by sells the cash price in exchange for waiting.

questions.question: A bakkie priced at R215 000 is financed with a deposit of R21 500, 72 monthly repayments of R3 285 and a balloon payment of R75 250. Calculate the total cost of the deal, state how much more than the price this is, and explain both why the instalment looks affordable and what the owner's options are when the balloon falls due.
questions.expected_answer: The repayments total 3 285 × 72 = R236 520. The full cost is deposit plus repayments plus balloon: 21 500 + 236 520 + 75 250 = R333 270, which is 333 270 − 215 000 = R118 270 more than the windscreen price. The instalment looks affordable because the balloon pushes R75 250 of the debt — 35% of the price — to the end of the term, so the monthly payments only carry the remaining debt and are therefore lower than an ordinary loan's would be. When month seventy-two arrives the balloon must still be dealt with, in one of three ways: pay the R75 250 as a lump sum, refinance it into a new loan and pay new interest on old debt, or sell the bakkie to settle it. The deal should be judged on the total of everything ever paid, not on the monthly figure.

questions.question: A R18 000 personal loan runs 24 months at R939 per month, with a R60 monthly service fee and a R1 050 initiation fee. Calculate the total cost of credit. Then, for a vehicle policy with a R5 200 excess, calculate the payout on damage of R31 400 and explain what the excess is for.
questions.expected_answer: The true monthly outflow is 939 + 60 = R999. The total paid is the initiation fee plus 24 months of that outflow: 1 050 + 24 × 999 = 1 050 + 23 976 = R25 026,00. The total cost of credit is everything paid minus the cash received: 25 026 − 18 000 = R7 026,00, which is about 39% of the amount borrowed — every fee counts, not only the advertised repayment. On the insurance claim, the insurer pays the damage minus the excess: 31 400 − 5 200 = R26 200, while the owner pays the first R5 200 personally. The excess keeps small claims out of the system, which keeps premiums lower for everyone, and it gives the owner a reason to avoid careless small losses; on a financed vehicle the bank usually requires this insurance because the vehicle is its security until the debt, including any balloon, is settled.
